name: Columbia Valley Local Conservation Fund
summary: A local parcel-tax conservation fund in British Columbia's Columbia Valley that pays for projects addressing a known threat to biodiversity, such as ecosystem restoration and invasive species control. Land trusts can apply for securement at any time.

geography.label: Columbia Valley, BC (Spillimacheen to Canal Flats)

steps: Proposal (land acquisitions and covenants: any time)

eligibility.rule: Project is in the Fund Service Area
Project addresses IUCN threats to biodiversity targets and a theme area
Multi-year project lasts no more than three years
Project is not a listed ineligible activity

status.quote: Current Intake General 2027 project applications are currently being reviewed.

calls.label: Land trust acquisition or covenant projects (ongoing)

status.quote: Due to time sensitivity of securement projects, these applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

calls.note: Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis

administered_by.quote: We partner with the Regional District of East Kootenay (RDEK) to support funding for projects in rural areas and municipalities in the Columbia Valley

applicant_types.quote: Applications are accepted from the following: Registered non-profit organizations; First Nations; Local governments.

geography.quote: We partner with the Regional District of East Kootenay (RDEK) to support funding for projects in rural areas and municipalities in the Columbia Valley, between Spillimacheen and Canal Flats.

access.quote: Applications are accepted from the following: Registered non-profit organizations; First Nations; Local governments.

effort.quote: Land acquisition or covenant proposals may be submitted at any time during the year provided there is sufficient time for the Technical Review Committee and RDEK to review the proposals.

eligibility.quote: (3) Projects must be in the Fund Service Area.
(5) Projects must address IUCN threats to biodiversity targets and fall into at least one theme area (see Section 4).
(4) Multi-year projects are acceptable to a maximum of three years.

The following types of projects will not be considered for funding: (a) Projects that relieve any level of government of its obligations (projects may augment or enhance government activities); (b) Capacity building or operating expenses for organizations; (c) Projects with recreational benefits only; (d) Community infrastructure services;

after_award.quote: 25% upon completion of the approved final report.
Proponents must be prepared to make a 10-minute presentation on the outcomes of their work on an annual basis, in addition to submitting a written report.
